close_reason:
Fixed bd-spin and /do-beads.

bd-spin (~/bin/bd-spin):
- count_open_ready, count_open_blocked, count_in_progress, count_human_needed now use --limit 0 to get true counts (were silently capped at bd's default limit, 10 for ready and 50 for list)
- Added count_open_ready_non_human helper that filters out human-labeled beads via jq
- Renamed verdict semantics: human_needed now fires only when POST_READY_NON_HUMAN == 0 AND POST_HUMAN > 0, not on any human-labeled bead existing
- Pre-loop and pre-session checks gate on POST_READY_NON_HUMAN, not raw POST_READY
- Summary JSON gained initial_ready_non_human and final_ready_non_human fields
- bd-spin --last bead-flow table shows both 'Ready (all)' and 'Ready (non-human)' rows
- Updated docstring, --help, --prime, and --last interpretation strings
- Added explicit case-statement arms for all_blocked, all_claimed_at_start, empty_at_start verdicts in --last (were previously falling through to drained's interpretation)

/do-beads (~/.config/opencode/commands/do-beads.md):
- Step 1 now uses jq to filter out human-labeled beads from bd ready output (otherwise the inner agent picks the same question-bead every session and never makes progress)
- Step 1 documents the null-return case: when every ready bead is human-labeled, exit cleanly and let bd-spin's outer loop surface the human_needed verdict
- Parallel-work fan-out section updated to use the same human-filter jq pipeline

Verified with bd-spin --dry-run: loop now reports 'ready=45 (non-human=44)' and keeps spinning past JMAP-ltx4 instead of halting after session 1.
description:
bd-spin's post-session check at line 949 stops when POST_HUMAN > 0, regardless of whether non-human ready work remains. The intent of the 'turn questions into beads' workflow is file-and-continue, but the outer loop treats the human label as a global halt.

Also: count_open_ready, count_open_blocked, count_in_progress, count_human_needed all omit --limit, so bd's default limit caps them silently (ready=10, list=50). This makes the logged ready/blocked/inprogress counts inaccurate when there are more than the defaults.

Fix:
1. Add explicit --limit 0 (unlimited) to all count_* helpers
2. Add count_open_ready_non_human helper that filters out 'human'-labeled beads via jq
3. Change stop condition to: stop only when count_open_ready_non_human == 0 AND human > 0
4. Update pre-loop and in-loop checks symmetrically
5. Update log messages to surface non-human-ready

Also update ~/.config/opencode/commands/do-beads.md step 1 to filter out human-labeled beads when picking the next bead, so the inner agent doesn't waste a round trip claiming-then-rejecting them.

User-visible context: previous bd-spin run on JMAP-ltx4 stalled the entire frontier (45 ready beads) because one bead (JMAP-ltx4) carries the human label.
title: bd-spin halts on any human-labeled bead instead of working around it
